name: GLSL
summary: C-like shading language for programmable stages of the OpenGL graphics pipeline (vertex, tessellation, geometry, fragment, compute), introduced with OpenGL 2.0 and maintained by Khronos; GLSL ES is the OpenGL ES/WebGL dialect, and GLSL with GL_KHR_vulkan_glsl compiles to SPIR-V for Vulkan. Provides vector/matrix types, opaque sampler/image types, storage and layout qualifiers and a large built-in function library.

level_notes.1: The Khronos specifications (GLSL 4.60, GLSL ES 3.20) are free HTML/PDF in the Khronos registry; it sits behind a bot challenge so the link checker reports these URLs as blocked. Section anchors were taken from the explicit [[ids]] in the AsciiDoc spec source (KhronosGroup/GLSL), which is also linked directly.
level_notes.0: glslang is the Khronos reference front end (GLSL/ESSL to SPIR-V). Other implementations: Mesa GLSL compiler, ANGLE shader translator, naga (wgpu) GLSL front/back end, SPIRV-Cross (SPIR-V to GLSL), shaderc.
level_notes.2: Many free tutorials (LearnOpenGL, The Book of Shaders, WebGL2 Fundamentals, MDN); the OpenGL Wiki pages are also behind the Khronos bot challenge.
